answer: In this PoA design, identity verification binds each claimant to a VDF whose challenge seeds a chain of sequential modular squarings, with a Wesolowski proof attesting the required work. A sybil operator may create many nominal clones, but cannot shorten any clone’s dependency chain by distributing it across GPUs: every square depends on the preceding result. This strict physical time bottleneck makes mass identities costly, while an anchor, umber-tagged record, and cipher protect identity linkage.
